newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenian interior minister says order restored.
newsitem.headline: Armenian interior minister says order restored.

text.p: Armenian Interior Minister Vanik Siradegyan said on Wednesday police had restored order in the capital Yerevan after clashes with protesters contesting President Levon Ter-Petrosyan's election victory.

Siradegyan said in a brief television address to the nation that police had fired shots to disperse a crowd which converged on the parliament building but that no one had been killed. He also appealed for people to remain calm and stay at home.
The minister repeated accusations made earlier by a presidential spokesman that the protests amounted to an attempted coup d'etat.
"We were able to stop this wave of violence after the forces of public order fired into the air," Siradegyan said. "Fortunately there were no victims."
He said parliamentary speaker Babken Ararktsyan had been beaten during the incident and treated in hospital.

Violence spilled over at a protest by tens of thousands of demonstrators who say Sunday's election in the Caucasian republic was rigged and that the real winner was former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan. The authorities deny the accusations.
